items.title: 68516_Gene Ramey oral history interview
items.q: I had my uncle John, married to a lady by the name of Leela Johnson, who was the first cousin of Jack Johnson, the prize fighter.

ctx.x: What did he do after that?

Well, he sang in the quartet, and he took a job as a shoeshine boy. He worked at odd jobs, and things. But that was about his only talent, because I think he left school in the 6th grade. You know, in those days, when Jack Johnson became king, everybody -- so I had two brother-in-laws who were prize fighters, or wanted to be prize fighters.

And one of them I remember very well, because he was the joker of the whole town. Now, these things that Sugar Ray developed, in the forties, evidently he was on his way out to do that. But he's a heavyweight. So they say he would throw one punch, and do all kinds of dancing up and down, and somebody caught him when he was up in the air, knocked him all the way out of the ring. That ended his career. But they called him Pip Sweeney. But he was -- they say he put on quite a show. He'd swing one punch and miss you…
